mainTopic: Refuting the קל וחומר for בשר בחלב, benefit from בשר בחלב, and whether wild animals and birds are included
overview: The גמרא is defending a קל וחומר that בשר בחלב is forbidden for benefit, learned from things like כלאי הכרם. First it sets rules for how strong a refutation (פירכא) must be, depending on whether the proof comes from one, two or three sources. Next it asks whether כלאי הכרם are different because they were never permitted. רב אדא בר אהבה answers that even the original seed becomes forbidden, and it was permitted before it took root. A משנה about a perforated pot seems to disagree, and אביי resolves it with two words in the פסוק. The גמרא then notes that רבי שמעון disagrees with our משנה and permits benefit from בשר בחלב, learning from טריפה. It goes on to explain רבי עקיבא's and רבי יוסי הגלילי's views on wild animals and birds with milk. A ברייתא and a story about לוי show that some towns ate bird with milk. Finally a new משנה begins about using an animal's stomach (קיבה) to make cheese. Its ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How strong a refutation must be: one source vs. two sources
steps.stepSummary: When a קל וחומר is learned from one source, you need a real קולא וחומרא to refute it. When it is learned from two sources, even any small difference refutes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we learn one thing from one other thing, we can only refute it by showing a leniency and a stringency, not with just any difference. When we learn one thing from two things, we can refute it even with just any difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the rules for how strong a refutation (פירכא) needs to be in order to knock down a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the proof comes from only one source, a small, random difference is not enough. You must show that the source is stricter in one way and more lenient in another (קולא וחומרא). If the proof comes from two sources, it is weaker, so even a small difference (כל דהו) can break it.

keyTerms.meaning: We refute (we raise a פירכא, an objection that breaks the proof)
A leniency and a stringency: showing the source is lenient in one way but strict in another
Anything at all; any small difference
One from two: learning one law from two sources

phrases.english: When learning one from one,
we refute with a leniency and a stringency;
we do not refute with just any difference.
When learning one from two,
we refute even with just any difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (from before this section) about refuting the קל וחומר for בשר בחלב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From one source: refute only with קולא וחומרא. From two sources: refute even with any difference.

steps.title: How strong a refutation must be: one source vs. three sources
steps.stepSummary: When learning from three sources, if the argument goes around and relies on the common factor (במה הצד), any difference refutes it. If not, only a real קולא וחומרא refutes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we learn one thing from three things: if the argument goes around and we end up using 'the common side' of all of them, we can refute with any difference. But if not, we can only refute with a leniency and a stringency, not with just any difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of refutation rules, now for a proof built on three sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each of the three sources can be knocked down on its own, the argument keeps going in a circle and ends up relying only on what they share (במה הצד); then any shared difference is enough to break it. If the argument does not go around like that, the proof is stronger, and you need a real קולא וחומרא. This explains why the earlier small objection (that all the sources grow from the ground) did not knock down the proof for בשר בחלב.

keyTerms.meaning: One from three: learning one law from three sources
The argument goes back around in a circle
'What is the common side': a proof based on what several sources share

steps.whatToRemember: The more the proof depends on sources leaning on each other, the weaker it is, and the smaller the objection needed to break it.

phrases.english: When learning one from three,
if the argument goes back around
and comes through 'the common side,'
phrases.notes: The proof ends up resting only on what the sources have in common, since each one alone can be knocked down.

phrases.english: we refute with any difference;
and if not,
we refute with a leniency and a stringency;
we do not refute with just any difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מִתְּלָת, אִי הָדַר דִּינָא וְאָתֵי בְּמָה הַצַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of refutation rules begun in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From three sources: if the argument goes around to במה הצד, any difference refutes; otherwise only קולא וחומרא refutes.

steps.title: New objection: כלאי הכרם were never permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests breaking the proof by saying כלאי הכרם are different, because they never had a time when they were permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us refute it: what about כלאי הכרם? They are different, because they never had a time when they were permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we don't knock down the proof from כלאי הכרם with a real difference: they were forbidden from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat and milk were each permitted before being cooked together. כלאי הכרם seem forbidden as soon as they grow, so they never had a permitted stage (שעת הכושר). That makes them stricter in a real way, which might be enough to break the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us refute; why not raise this objection?
Forbidden mixed plantings in a vineyard
A time when the item was fit and permitted

phrases.english: But let us refute:
What about diverse kinds in a vineyard?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הָיְתָה לָהֶן שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר?
phrases.english: They are different, for they never had a time when they were fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the proof from a small objection, the גמרא raises a stronger kind of objection.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר that learns בשר בחלב from כלאי הכרם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כלאי הכרם were never permitted, unlike meat and milk, so they are stricter and cannot teach about בשר בחלב.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: the original seed is forbidden too, and it was once permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה learns from the fact that this objection was not raised that even the original seed of כלאי הכרם becomes forbidden, and it was permitted before it took root.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: This teaches that the original plant of כלאי הכרם becomes forbidden, and it had a time when it was fit, before it took root.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers the objection by saying כלאי הכרם did have a permitted stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this objection was not used, it must not be true. That means not only the new growth is forbidden, but also the original seed or sapling (עיקרן). That seed was permitted before it took root, so כלאי הכרם did have a שעת הכושר.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches; we can learn from here
Their original part (the seed or sapling itself) becomes forbidden
Taking root

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a new הלכה about כלאי הכרם: the forbidden status reaches back to the original seed, not just the new growth.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
This teaches
that with diverse kinds in a vineyard, the original plant becomes forbidden,
and they had a time when they were fit
before taking root.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the factual premise of the objection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כלאי הכרם are forbidden from their first growth, so they never had a permitted stage.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the original seed becomes forbidden, and it was permitted before rooting, so there was a שעת הכושר.

steps.title: Challenge from the perforated pot carried through a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה בר זעירא brings a משנה that suggests only the new growth is forbidden, not the original plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה בר זעירא objected: One who carries a pot with a hole in it through a vineyard, if the plant grew by one part in two hundred, it is forbidden. If it grew, yes; if it did not grow, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה בר זעירא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה from a משנה about a perforated pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids the plant only if it grew enough. That implies that if it did not grow, it stays permitted. So the original plant itself does not become forbidden, only the new growth, which goes against רב אדא בר אהבה's claim that עיקרן נאסר.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant pot with a hole, so it counts as planted in the ground
Grew by one part in two hundred
Yes / no: the גמרא's way of drawing an inference from the wording

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not from what the משנה says outright, but from what it implies: 'if it grew' means that without growth, the plant is permitted.

phrases.english: Rav Shemaya bar Zeira objected:
One who carries a perforated pot through a vineyard,
if it grew by a two-hundredth, it is forbidden.
If it grew, yes,
if it did not grow, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of רב אדא בר אהבה in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's claim that the original plant of כלאי הכרם becomes forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that without new growth the plant stays permitted, so only the growth is forbidden, not the original plant.

steps.title: אביי: Two words in the פסוק, two different cases
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the פסוק of כלאי הכרם hints at two rules. A seed planted in the vineyard is forbidden once it takes root. A plant brought in from elsewhere is forbidden only if it grows there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There are two separate words written in the פסוק. It says 'lest the growth be forbidden,' and it says 'the seed.' How do these fit together? If it was planted in the vineyard from the start, it becomes forbidden as soon as it takes root. If it was planted elsewhere and brought in: if it grew, yes, it is forbidden; if it did not grow, no.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from the משנה in step 5. He shows that the משנה is only talking about a plant that was brought into the vineyard from outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'seed' teaches that a seed planted in the vineyard becomes forbidden itself once it roots. The word 'growth' teaches that a plant brought in from outside is forbidden only through new growth, and that second case is what the משנה in step 5 means. So רב אדא בר אהבה is right that the original seed can become forbidden, even though it was permitted before it rooted.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes forbidden (here, forbidden as כלאי הכרם)
How can these fit together? (a phrase that resolves two sources)
Taking root
Planted elsewhere and then brought into the vineyard
It grew (added size)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say that only new growth is ever forbidden. That rule applies only to a plant brought in from outside. A seed planted right in the vineyard is itself forbidden once it roots.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps alive the point from step 4 that כלאי הכרם was once permitted. That point is needed for the earlier proof about בשר בחלב.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Two verses are written,
phrases.notes: He really means two separate phrases inside one פסוק, דברים 22:9.

phrases.english: it is written: "Lest the growth be forbidden,"
and it is written: "the seed."
How do these fit together?
If it was planted there from the start, it is forbidden upon taking root;
if it was planted elsewhere and brought in,
if it grew, yes, it is forbidden,
if it did not grow, no, it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the משנה brought by רב שמעיה בר זעירא in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two cases (אוקימתא), based on two words in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that only new growth is ever forbidden, never the original seed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A seed planted in the vineyard is forbidden upon rooting. A plant brought in from outside is forbidden only if it grows. The משנה is talking about the second case.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון, who permits benefit from בשר בחלב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that our משנה, which forbids benefit from בשר בחלב, disagrees with a ברייתא. There רבי שמעון learns from טריפה that בשר בחלב is only forbidden to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow this תנא. It was taught: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: בשר בחלב is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit. It says, 'For you are a holy people' (about בשר בחלב), and elsewhere it says, 'And you shall be holy people to Me' (about טריפה). Just as there it is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit, so too here it is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that there is a תנא who disagrees with our משנה and allows benefit from בשר בחלב. It quotes his ברייתא and his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון links the word 'holy' in the פסוק of בשר בחלב with 'holy' in the פסוק of טריפה (a גזירה שוה). The טריפה פסוק says to throw it to the dogs, so benefit from it is allowed. He reasons that בשר בחלב, like טריפה, is forbidden only to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not follow the opinion of this תנא
Forbidden to eat
Permitted for benefit (for example, selling it or feeding it to animals)
An animal torn or fatally injured; forbidden to eat
Just as there, so too here (the pattern of a comparison between two פסוקים)
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two פסוקים

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה forbids benefit from בשר בחלב. רבי שמעון disagrees and permits benefit, learning from 'holy' in the פסוק of טריפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that whether one may benefit from בשר בחלב is an actual disagreement between תנאים.

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with this tanna,
phrases.notes: Our משנה is the one that says בשר בחלב is forbidden for benefit.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
Meat cooked in milk is forbidden to eat
but permitted for benefit,
as it is stated: "For you are a holy people,"
phrases.notes: דברים 14:21, the same פסוק that forbids cooking a kid in its mother's milk.

phrases.english: and it is stated elsewhere: "And you shall be holy people to Me."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:30. That פסוק goes on to say a טריפה should be thrown to the dogs.

phrases.english: Just as there it is forbidden to eat
but permitted for benefit,
so too here it is forbidden to eat
but permitted for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the proof that בשר בחלב is forbidden for benefit, the גמרא notes a תנא who disagrees with that ruling altogether.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, בשר בחלב is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit, learned from טריפה through the shared word 'holy.'

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's three verses were already used by שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's opinion from the משנה and objects. The three mentions of 'גדי' were already used for שמואל's teachings, so how can רבי עקיבא use them to exclude חיה, עוף and בהמה טמאה?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי עקיבא says a wild animal and a bird (are not forbidden with milk from the Torah). But those verses were already used up for the teaching of שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's line from the משנה and immediately challenges where he gets it from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא learns his rule from the fact that the Torah writes 'לא תבשל גדי' three times. But שמואל already used those same three mentions of 'גדי' to include other things in the prohibition. One verse can't easily serve two purposes, so it seems רבי עקיבא has no source left.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild (non-domesticated) kosher animal, like a deer
A bird
'They were taken out', meaning the verses were already used for something else

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is arguing with רבי עקיבא's הלכה itself. It is only asking where his source comes from, since the verses seem to be 'taken'.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: חַיָּה וָעוֹף וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: A wild animal and a bird, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה. רבי עקיבא learns from 'גדי' being written three times to leave out a wild animal, a bird, and a non-kosher animal.

phrases.english: But these verses, they were already taken out (used)
for the teaching of Shmuel!
phrases.notes: שמואל taught earlier that the three mentions of 'גדי' include forbidden fat, a dead animal, and a fetus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the debate about benefit (step 7) to the next part of the משנה, רבי עקיבא's exclusions.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's derivation from the three mentions of 'גדי'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same three verses are already needed for שמואל's three teachings, so they are not free to exclude חיה, עוף and בהמה טמאה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא doesn't need the verses for שמואל's teachings
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that one prohibition can take effect on another, so חלב and מתה need no verse. A fetus is a regular kid anyway, so it needs no verse either. All three verses are free to exclude חיה, עוף and בהמה טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds that a prohibition can take effect on top of another prohibition. So forbidden fat and a dead animal don't need a verse to be included. A fetus is a full-fledged kid. So all three verses are left over to exclude a wild animal, a bird, and a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that, according to רבי עקיבא, שמואל's three teachings don't need any verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל needed verses because otherwise we might think בשר בחלב can't take effect on meat that is already forbidden (חלב, a dead animal). רבי עקיבא holds איסור חל על איסור, so that is automatic. A שליל is simply a real kid, so it is included without a verse. That leaves all three 'גדי' verses free for exclusions.

keyTerms.meaning: A new prohibition can take effect on something that is already forbidden
Forbidden fat of an animal
An animal that died without proper שחיטה (נבלה)
A fetus found inside a slaughtered animal
They are extra, left over for another lesson
A non-kosher animal

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a broader opinion (איסור חל על איסור) can free up verses for new lessons. Whether a verse is 'needed' depends on each תנא's other views.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds:
a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition,
so forbidden fat and a dead animal don't need a verse,
phrases.notes: They are already forbidden, but for him בשר בחלב still takes effect on them automatically.

phrases.english: a fetus is a full-fledged kid,
so all of them (the verses) are left over
to exclude a wild animal, a bird, and a non-kosher animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the verses are not needed for the other teachings according to this תנא's views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three 'גדי' verses are used up by שמואל's teachings.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי עקיבא, שמואל's cases need no verse, so all three verses exclude חיה, עוף and בהמה טמאה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: three times 'גדי' means three exclusions (חיה, עוף, בהמה טמאה), because איסור חל על איסור and a שליל is a real kid.

steps.title: How does רבי יוסי הגלילי differ from רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי הגלילי from the משנה. He also leaves out a bird, just from a different verse. It asks what practical difference there is between the two views.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: It is said 'You shall not eat' (any נבלה). What practical difference is there between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי הגלילי's opinion and asks what the practical difference is between him and רבי עקיבא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that a bird is not forbidden with milk from the Torah. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns it from 'בחלב אמו', since a bird has no mother's milk. Since the result for a bird is the same, the גמרא wants to know where they actually disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall not eat': the start of the פסוק about נבלה that sits next to 'לא תבשל גדי'
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
'What is the difference between': asking for the practical difference between two opinions

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
It is stated: 'You shall not eat.'
phrases.notes: דברים 14:21. The משנה continues: a bird is left out because the פסוק says 'in its mother's milk', and a bird has no mother's milk.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא?
phrases.english: What difference is there between Rabbi Yosei HaGelili and Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After securing רבי עקיבא's source, the גמרא compares him to the next opinion in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא, since both exclude a bird.

steps.title: The difference is a wild animal
steps.stepSummary: They differ about חיה. For רבי יוסי הגלילי, meat of a חיה with milk is forbidden from the Torah. For רבי עקיבא it is only forbidden מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a wild animal. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds a wild animal is forbidden from the Torah, and רבי עקיבא holds a wild animal is only forbidden by the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two תנאים argue about a wild animal (חיה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי only leaves out what has no 'mother's milk'. A חיה does have mother's milk, so it stays forbidden from the Torah. רבי עקיבא's verses directly exclude חיה, so for him it is only a rabbinic prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is between them': introduces the practical difference
From the Torah
From the Rabbis (a rabbinic law)

steps.whatToRemember: Bird: both say not from the Torah. Wild animal: רבי יוסי הגלילי says from the Torah, and רבי עקיבא says only מדרבנן.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: a wild animal.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי סָבַר חַיָּה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds a wild animal is forbidden by Torah law,
and Rabbi Akiva holds a wild animal is forbidden only by rabbinic law.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ about חיה. It is forbidden from the Torah for רבי יוסי הגלילי and only rabbinically for רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: A second answer: they differ about bird meat
steps.stepSummary: Another option: the difference is about עוף. רבי עקיבא forbids it מדרבנן. רבי יוסי הגלילי does not forbid it even מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say the difference between them is a bird. רבי עקיבא holds that חיה and עוף are not forbidden from the Torah, but they are forbidden מדרבנן. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that a bird is not forbidden even מדרבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer to the question from step 10 about what difference there is between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the difference was חיה. Now the גמרא says the difference can be עוף. Both agree a bird is not forbidden from the Torah. But רבי עקיבא's words 'not from the Torah' hint that the רבנן did forbid it, while רבי יוסי הגלילי allows bird with milk completely.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces a second, different answer)
There is a difference between them
From the Torah itself
Forbidden by the Sages, not by the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי agree that bird with milk is NOT a Torah prohibition. They only argue about whether the רבנן added a prohibition.

phrases.english: If you want, say: a bird is the difference between them:
Rabbi Akiva holds
a wild animal and a bird are not forbidden from the Torah,
which means that by rabbinic law they are forbidden,
and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds

phrases.aramaic: עוֹף אֲפִילּוּ מִדְּרַבָּנַן נָמֵי לָא אֲסִיר.
phrases.english: a bird is not forbidden, not even by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question in step 10, instead of the חיה answer in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the practical difference between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bird meat with milk: forbidden מדרבנן for רבי עקיבא, fully permitted for רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי's town ate bird with milk
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that in רבי יוסי הגלילי's town people ate bird meat with milk. So he did not forbid it even מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: in רבי אליעזר's place they would cut trees to make charcoal to make iron. In רבי יוסי הגלילי's place they would eat bird meat with milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the second answer: רבי יוסי הגלילי allows bird with milk completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a rabbinic prohibition applied, a whole town would not openly eat bird with milk. The ברייתא lists towns that acted on their own רב's lenient view. It shows רבי יוסי הגלילי's view was actually followed in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: In his place, the town where that רב was the authority
Charcoal
Bird meat cooked with milk

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a town may follow its own local רב's ruling, even when others disagree. That idea comes back in the next story with לוי.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a baraita:
In the place of Rabbi Eliezer
they would cut down trees
to make charcoal to make iron,
phrases.notes: This was on שבת, to make a knife for a ברית מילה. רבי אליעזר holds that even these preparations push aside שבת.

phrases.english: in the place of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili
they would eat bird meat with milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 12's claim that רבי יוסי הגלילי allows bird with milk even מדרבנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי הגלילי does not forbid bird with milk at all.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying people openly ate bird with milk in his town.

steps.title: לוי is served peacock in milk, and רבי asks why he was silent
steps.stepSummary: לוי was served a peacock head cooked in milk and said nothing. רבי asked him why he did not put them in שמתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי came to the house of יוסף the bird hunter. They served him a peacock head in milk, and he said nothing to them. When he came before רבי, רבי said to him: Why did you not put them in שמתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רבי challenges לוי for keeping quiet when people ate bird with milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי assumes bird with milk is forbidden מדרבנן, like רבי עקיבא. So people who openly break it deserve שמתא. His question sets up לוי's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Bird hunter
Peacock
Put them in שַׁמְתָּא, a kind of ban or excommunication

phrases.english: Levi happened to come to the house of Yosef the bird hunter,
they brought before him
the head of a peacock in milk,
and he did not say anything at all to them.
When he came before Rabbi,
he said to him: Why did you not put them in a ban?
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא. He is the one asking לוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that applies the bird-with-milk dispute in real life.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's silence when he saw bird cooked in milk.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bird with milk is forbidden מדרבנן, so openly eating it deserves שמתא.

steps.title: לוי explains: the town may follow רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: לוי answers that this was רבי יהודה בן בתירא's town. He may have taught them like רבי יוסי הגלילי, who leaves out bird, since a bird has no mother's milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is the place of רבי יהודה בן בתירא. I said to myself: maybe he taught them like רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said: bird is left out, because it has no mother's milk.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי defends his silence. The people may have been following their local רב, who could have ruled like רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from 'its mother's milk' that bird is left out, because a bird does not nurse. If the local רב taught that, the people were following a real opinion. So לוי could not punish them.

keyTerms.meaning: His place, the town where a רב is the authority
He taught or explained from the פסוק
Mother's milk

steps.whatToRemember: Bird with milk: not forbidden from the Torah according to both. רבי עקיבא forbids it מדרבנן. רבי יוסי הגלילי allows it completely, because a bird has no mother's milk. A town that follows its own רב's ruling is not punished for it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא הוּא,
phrases.english: He said to him: It is the place of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמֵינָא: דְּרַשׁ לְהוּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי,
phrases.english: and I said: maybe he taught them like Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: יָצָא עוֹף שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֲלֵב אֵם.
phrases.english: who said: a bird is left out, since it has no mother's milk.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading of 'בחלב אמו' (שמות 23:19), from the משנה in step 10.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא הוּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Local custom follows a valid opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Openly eating bird with milk deserves שמתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the town may follow רבי יוסי הגלילי through its local רב, they cannot be punished.

steps.title: The stomach of a non-Jew's animal or a carcass is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that קיבה from an animal of a גוי, or from a נבלה, is אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The stomach of a non-Jew's animal, and the stomach of a carcass, is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that קיבה taken from a גוי's animal or from a נבלה may not be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קיבה was used to curdle milk into cheese. The משנה rules that if it comes from an animal that was not properly slaughtered, such as a נבלה or an animal of a גוי, it is forbidden. This is a clear starting rule for the new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the base text the גמרא will discuss
The stomach of an animal, or the curdled milk inside it, used to make cheese
An animal that died without a kosher slaughter
Forbidden

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The stomach of a non-Jew's animal, and that of a carcass
phrases.notes: Here קיבה means the curdled milk found in the animal's stomach, which people used to make cheese.

phrases.english: is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ קֵבַת גּוֹי וְשֶׁל נְבֵלָה הֲרֵי זוֹ אֲסוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It does not continue the עוף בחלב discussion of steps 11-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קיבה from an animal of a גוי or from a נבלה is forbidden.

steps.title: Setting up the case of curdling with a kosher stomach's skin
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a second case: someone who curdles milk using the skin of a kosher animal's stomach. The ruling comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who curdles milk using the skin of the stomach of a kosher animal...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its next case. It describes someone making cheese with the stomach skin of a kosher animal, and the ruling will come in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the animal is כשרה, so the problem is not נבלה. The question is about meat and milk: the stomach skin is meat, and it was used to curdle milk. The משנה has not given its answer yet.

keyTerms.meaning: One who curdles milk, making it set into cheese
The skin or wall of the stomach itself, not the milk inside it
A kosher animal that was properly slaughtered

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two cases. The first was about a forbidden animal. This one is a kosher animal, and the concern is meat mixing with milk. The ruling has not come yet.

phrases.english: One who curdles milk with the skin
of the stomach of a kosher animal,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a forbidden animal's קיבה to a new case with a kosher animal's stomach skin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup only: curdling milk with the stomach skin of a kosher animal. The ruling follows in the next part of the text.
